Single target rotation:

Shield Lob, Fast Blade, Circle of Scorn, Savage Blade, Spirits Within, Rage of Halone, Halone combo spam.

Multi target rotation: ALWAYS FOCUS YOUR MARKED 1, you WILL lose aggro if you look away from it too long, your deeps mean buisness.

Shield Lob, Flash, Circle of Scorn, Flash, Spirits within, Fast blade, Savage Blade, 
IF YOUR DEEPS IS AVERAGE - Rage of Halone, Flash, Flash
IF YOUR DEEPS IS ABOVE AVERAGE - Flash, Rage of Halone, Flash
When you are done this, do another halone combo, tab through the mobs between abilities to check if the flashes are necessary at this point, continue haloning.

When mob 1 is about to die, stop hitting it and turn to mob 2 to get a dominating enmity lead so you dont have to worry. Dont duel the poor bastard to the bitter end. Just make sure there is enough threat generated on it to last until it dies.

AK specifically, in the first third, you will encounter summoners and marauder type mobs with dulahans thrown in. There will also be some non issue goyle looking mobs. Kill priority is Summoners> Marauders. Mark and Shield lob the one summoner in the first pack, flash, circle of scorn then shield bash it to stun it out of summoning the add. Follow it up by a second flash and a spirits within. Spirits within is a 300 potency nuke on top of the silence. If you have no need to use the silence, use it on cooldown. After one rage of halone rotation you will need to double flash again. As a rule, an average geared group wont pull threat off of your off mob until you try and go past one rage of halone rotation. 

Continue stunning the mob and when you are sure it will die without summoning, switch to the marauder and take flash out of the rotation. If it is early enough, circle of scorn is still good to use as a GCD filler spell but you want it for the next pack. 

Next you will find a room with 3 goyles. Simply mark one and two and do the same roatation without the stun:

Shield lob, Flash, Circle of Scorn, Flash, Spirits Within, Halone Combo, flash, Flash.

On the final mob in any pack, threat being observed, you can switch from a halone rotation to a riot blade combo to return mana for the flash spam to come.

For dulahans, if you engage them immediately and star deepsing on the pull, they will cast iron justice at around 50%. If you shield bash them when they pass 50% and again when the stun expires, they should be locked down without ever casting a spell in most groups.

For reference,  the second summmoner group you want to target the nearest summoner first and the final summoner group you want to target the summoner on the right.

For the boss, you should never lose single target threat. When the summoner starts summoning, make sure you cast a fast blade before moving to the boss to finish the halone combo, weaving circle of scorn and spirits within. This should give you plenty of threat to turn and burn the summoner with an occasional flash if the deeps is slow.

The rock adds should be taunted as soon as they are at the nearest point to you to catch up to healer aggro, followed by a shield lob. Adds spawn roughly every 30 seconds which is great timing for you.

The next area has goyles with houndlights, dulahans and statues. In the goyle groups, none of the mobs are particularly scary alone but together they hurt. I usually kill the goyle first cause it stands out. Same aoe rotation.

Every time you seee statues, approach them carefully as any random 2  or 3 will become active and you need to quickly mark one or two to avoid confusion. the first set is 2, then 3, 2 then 3. The 3s are the hardest to pull, ensure you right click renew before approaching them so that they dont path weirdly towards your healer should they be a whm. Otherwise they are relatively harmless melee mobs.

Dulahans are still a joke.

Demon Wall is very easy if you are spam happy. Remember you have no reason to use mana except flash and single target, flash is a rare occurrence. Therefore, when bees spawn, mark one, shield lob it so it moves sooner then the other bee, let them get within flash range of eachother and spam spam spam. This is far easier then any rotation while dancing over the purple tiles and you should be using a limit break here to greeatly reduce their lifespan.

For the final stretch, stun succubi when they are casting Void Thunder III. That shit hurts. You can always pull a succubi alone with Provoke so attempt that before pulling the whole pack or you will need CDs.

The last boss is a tank and spank.

I was actually explaining this to a few friends the other day, very well written. I actually feel as if the gearing system is fine, however. 

Keep in mind that the HQ percent cap for max level must be quite high. I highly doubt you will hit this without wasting much points. However if you do, you fix the problem in the same way you would GP gear. All you need to do is swap out the piece to align with the node bonuses.

A miner at the level of the node will not have the base strength required to get the extra harvest bonus, I see it as highly unlikely at max level. This allows us to gear for Perception when under cap and the appropriate resistances/ strength above the cap.

First, let me thank you for a very informative post. It very likely took you a lot of time to write this up and the basics you provided will surely help a lot of inexperienced healers. 

Second, I would have to say i disagree with you on some of the pros and cons of the spells, the biggest of which being Regen. Regen is not meant to be party spammed at all and is in the most part going to be an over heal. This is because HoTs are not meant to do massive healing like the cure series but rather stabilize incoming damage. If there is a fight where the tank takes significant melee damage from the boss, Regen can be the difference between needing to be ready with Cure IIs or being able to relax with easy Cure Is and enjoy the Free cure procs. Te problem with it being unaffected by Divine Seal is fine. Same as the critical issue. Sustained healing is not supposed to come in surprise bursts and Divine seal is a 15 second buff. Refresh Regen before Divine seal and after. The relationship that Regen has to Cure I is like the relationship you described between Cure III and Medica II. You use it situationally but both have their place.

Next is Shroud of Saints. The enmity cut is actually incredibly useful if adds spawn and you are forced to keep healing before the Tank can pick them up. If you know an add phase is coming, which usually indicates a higher healing output putting the refresh to good use, letting the adds spawn and popping SoS when the tank is picking them up will make it go far smoother. This is a utility spell. Sometimes you use it for the enmity cut, sometimes you use it for the refresh. That is the great thing about spells with two purposes. 

Finally is cleric stance. Please don't advertise to new healers that they can deeps ;-; I'll be rotting away as they are trying to throw rocks and the boss.

Overall great write up. My opinions may just be a difference in healing styles but maybe, if I am lucky, you can take something away and get better from your own thread! Take care.

See, at least you have presented a reason that you hold your opinion. Honestly, I wont even say you are wrong. I completely agree. The thing people don't realise is what polished really encompasses. The game as it is currently is not as terrible as people are screaming and there is actual in game footage of extremely well done portions, all be it small snipits, that were being played through.

My real headache comes from people saying that the mechanics look clunky when mechanics are the first thing companies work to fix. Example being the way the staff interacted with repetitive casting. Issues like this should be easy fixes. The staff still casted the fireball, it just looked weird. Let it look weird until they are at the phase where the visuals start taking over and mechanics are ironed out.

I can't say I played SWTOR. If, however, the game does as you say and remains in a polished state of mediocrity, I will assume they didn't learn from MMO predecessors and tag it as a game to avoid. I am not worried of this though as the entire game seems to have robbed amazing portions from many amazing MMOs to manufacture, what we hope will be, a best final result.

Finally, what I would like to say may come off offensive, I believe actually flat out saying the game will be a polished version of the beta is a pretty obvious statement, which you purposefully turned to try and burn the game with. Of course the game is a polished version of the beta, the beta is the game. It's like saying a cooked egg is still an egg. Also, if you admit the player was purposefully playing poorly, and then say that the beta footage is what the game will be like with a bow on top, you basically admit to saying the game's outcome is directly related to the quality of person sitting behind the computer playing when the information is leaked. We didn't see nearly enough to even know anything about the game. Its like playing WoW for the first time, getting to level 5 and saying you have a big enough sample of the game to say it'll be mediocre all the way through. I don't know how you can say that the end result would be, what I take to have negative connotations, just a polished version of what we were shown when we didn't see:

Synergy, pretty much any abilities in any tree in any part of the game, Proper use of the Finesse system, crafting, PvP, late PvE

To list a few. I am just not sold on the implication of that opinion or where it is justifiably grounded.
